edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: workers exposed to mixed organic solvents
edges.mechanism: Mixed organic-solvent exposure can include marrow-toxic compounds such as benzene, making leukemia a plausible downstream outcome in heavily exposed workers.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2020 Zhou meta analysis in BMC Public Health, which ties mixed organic-solvent exposure to leukemia in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
